description: A live mirror of github.com/elder-plinius as a searchable repo gallery AND a MARKET that turns every one of his repos into its own mod. Runs as three surfaces over one core: an API (:50592) that serves MCP at POST /mcp and, at POST /mcp/all, the same tools plus one per repo so a single connection covers every repo, an app (:50593) that holds no data, proxies /api/* to it and is drawn as an 8-bit console — square corners, hard offset shadows, scanlines, two bitmap faces (Press Start 2P and VT323) embedded as base64 woff2 so a page is one request, box-shadow pixel sprites instead of glyph icons, and every repo as a cartridge with a title bar filled in the accent — wearing any of 21 palettes (the BUILD console's set plus PLINY, ACID, VOID, BUBBLEGUM and HOT DOG) from the header's theme pill, and an stdio MCP server (mcp.py). The market ('install'/'stock') archives each repo's tree, README and readable files into the STORE mod (~/.mod/store/plinyville/*, content-addressed with a real localfs CID) and presents it as a self-contained mod at /m/<repo> with its own app, its own api and its own MCP server backend (/api/plinyville/m/<repo>/mcp) whose tools read that one repo offline. Also hosts a DEFANGED fork of his elder-plinius.github.io app ('plinyworld'), a clipboard-hijacking ('pastejacking') red-team PoC: the served page runs a neutralized trigger script that copies nothing and reveals, inline, what the live attack would have done. The original payload is preserved but unrun at plinyworld/upstream/triggers.js, served only as text/plain. The market archiver CLONES: 'install'/'stock' pull each repo over git ('gh repo clone' when the CLI is logged in, plain anonymous 'git' otherwise) and read the tree off disk, so one 'stock' run fills all 46 mods with no REST calls at all instead of dying at a 403; clones cache in ~/.mod/pliny/clones ('clones'/'forget_clones'), re-archiving only what moved, and 'via=api' still selects the old REST archiver. 'discover' re-lists the repos with no API budget either (gh repo list, else the public repositories page), which is what the daily scan and the app's refresh fall back to when the API says 403. The live mirror reads (repo/readme/tree/file/search on a repo that is not installed) are still GitHub REST calls. Anonymous GitHub is 60 requests/hour per IP, so a token is resolved per call from $GITHUB_TOKEN/$GH_TOKEN, this module's own secret at ~/.mod/pliny/github.json ('m pliny/token <pat>', validated and stored 0600, picked up by a running server with no restart), or the git mod's connected account; 'rate' reports the budget left and the app shows it when it runs low. 'update' re-pulls repos and the upstream snapshot. A cron job ('m pliny/cron', installed by 'deploy') scans once a day: it re-pulls the repos, re-pulls the plinyworld upstream, re-archives any installed mod whose repo moved, and re-mints the module's own registry CID. Every scan leaves a receipt in ~/.mod/pliny/scan.json, which the header pill and GET /status read — so the page says 'up to date · scanned 3h ago' (or that the last scan failed) and shows the CID of the code serving it. BUILD: three of these repos are apps that ship as source — a Vite index.html whose only script is /src/main.tsx loads blank — so the card offers the build upstream never ran (POST /m/<repo>/build, `m pliny/build <repo>`, pv_build): npm install with lifecycle scripts disabled, then the repo’s own build, and the built page becomes runnable like any other; a build that would only produce a page that throws (LEAKHUB wants a Convex deployment of its own) is refused before it starts, with the variable named. RUN: a third of these repos are not prose but browser apps (ST3GG, ImageDefender, R00TS, GLOSSOPETRAE, the 57 demos inside FABLE-SHOWCASE…), so each one runs under the mod: GET /m/<repo>/run/<path> serves it out of its clone with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` and no allow-same-origin, giving the page an opaque origin that cannot touch the one localStorage this host shares between mods — the header holds on a direct link, not just inside the console’s sandboxed iframe. The only edits to upstream are announced in the served source: an in-memory Storage shim (an opaque origin makes localStorage throw) and a provenance chip. Before you press RUN the page is audited — clipboard use, the hosts it calls, storage, camera, eval, an API key left in the source — and a repo that cannot run says why instead: a Vite entry the browser cannot compile, a front end for a localhost service, a corpus of prompts. elder-plinius.github.io is refused outright and points at the defanged exhibit. The market cards, GET /run, `m pliny/run` and the pv_run MCP tool all read the same index. TYPES: every repo is classified — jailbreak set, leaked system prompt, red-team tool, browser app, tool, writing, the exhibit, empty — with the evidence for every call, so GET /types, ?type= on every listing, the console’s pill row and the MCP tools all filter the wall down to one sort of thing. CHAT: POST /chat runs the headless CLAUDE AGENT against this module’s own MCP server (no Bash, no file tools, no other server, eleven read-only pv_* tools) and answers with the repo and path it read; a typed question fences the agent by starting that server with PLINYVILLE_SCOPE, so "find me jailbreaks" cannot open anything outside the thirteen jailbreak repos, and the fence is on the tool rather than in a prompt. The console streams every tool call as it happens (POST /chat/stream) and marks an answer that never opened a file as ungrounded.

endpoints.app: GET /plinyville — the market; /plinyville/m/<repo> — one mod; /plinyville/m/<repo>#run — that mod running; /plinyville/plinyworld — the exhibit
endpoints.clones: GET /api/plinyville/clones — the clone cache: what is checked out, at which commit, and whether the archive still matches
endpoints.discover: GET /api/plinyville/discover — re-list the repos without spending REST budget (gh, else the public repositories page)
endpoints.exhibit: GET /api/plinyville/exhibit — what the plinyworld PoC would do
endpoints.info: GET /api/plinyville — module info + route list (the null call)
endpoints.install: POST /api/plinyville/market/install?name= — archive one repo into the store by cloning it (name=* for all, via=api for the rate-limited REST archiver)
endpoints.market: GET /api/plinyville/market — the MARKET: every repo as its own mod
endpoints.mcp: POST /api/pliny/mcp — MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 (Streamable HTTP), the 11 corpus tools
endpoints.mcp_all: POST /api/pliny/mcp/all — the ALL server: the corpus tools plus one tool per elder-plinius repo (pv_<repo>), on one connection
endpoints.mod_api: GET /api/plinyville/m/<repo>/{readme,tree,file,search} — one mod's api (offline from the store)
endpoints.mod_mcp: POST /api/plinyville/m/<repo>/mcp — one mod's own MCP server
endpoints.payload: GET /api/plinyville/payload — the preserved payload, as text/plain
endpoints.rate: GET /api/plinyville/rate — GitHub rate-limit budget left + how we authenticate
endpoints.scan: POST /api/plinyville/scan — run the daily scan now (what the cron job runs once a day)
endpoints.status: GET /api/plinyville/status — the daily scan receipt: fresh or stale, what changed, and this module's own CID
endpoints.update: POST /api/plinyville/update — re-pull repos + the upstream snapshot
endpoints.run: GET /api/plinyville/run — the ARCADE: every repo that is an app, not a corpus
endpoints.mod_run: GET /api/plinyville/m/<repo>/run — can this repo run, from which entry, and what its scripts reach for; /run/<path> serves the app itself, sandboxed
endpoints.mod_audit: GET /api/plinyville/m/<repo>/audit — what the page touches: clipboard, hosts, storage, eval, a key in the source
endpoints.types: GET /api/plinyville/types — the taxonomy: what sort of thing each repo IS (jailbreak, system-prompt, redteam, app, tool, writing, exhibit, empty) with live counts; ?repo=<name> for one repo and the evidence behind every type it carries. The same ids filter /repos, /market and /run with ?type= (comma = AND)
endpoints.chat: POST /api/plinyville/chat {question, types?, repo?, model?, session?} — ask the corpus; the CLAUDE AGENT reads it through this module’s own MCP tools and answers with the repo and path. GET /chat is the agent/1.0 card
endpoints.chat_stream: POST /api/plinyville/chat/stream — the same as server-sent events: every tool call as it happens, then the answer
endpoints.agent_card: GET /api/plinyville/.well-known/agent.json — the agent/1.0 card: the model, the eleven read-only tools it may call, the scopes and the limits
endpoints.mod_types: GET /api/plinyville/m/<repo>/types — that repo’s types and why
endpoints.builds: GET /api/plinyville/builds — every build receipt, what is one build away from being playable, and what would still not work if it were built
endpoints.mod_build: GET /api/plinyville/m/<repo>/build — what building this repo would take, or how the last attempt went; POST to run it (returns at once, poll the GET)

exhibit_note: plinyworld is a DEFANGED clipboard-hijack red-team PoC hosted for study, not a live payload. See plinyworld/SOURCE.md.

market.archiver: git clone (clone.py) — `gh repo clone` when the CLI is logged in, plain anonymous `git` otherwise. The git transport is not on the REST API's 60-requests-an-hour anonymous budget, so `m pliny/stock` fills all 46 mods in one run instead of stopping at a 403; the REST archiver is still there as `via=api`.
market.clones: ~/.mod/pliny/clones — the working checkouts (a cache; the archive is the bundle in the store). `m pliny/clones` lists them, `m pliny/forget_clones` reclaims the disk.
market.discovery: `m pliny/discover` re-lists the repos with no REST calls at all (gh repo list, else the public repositories page) and merges into the gallery; the daily scan falls back to it when the API says 403.
market.note: every elder-plinius repo, archived into the STORE mod and served as its own mod (app+api+mcp) at /m/<repo>; content-addressed with a real localfs CID

all.connect: claude mcp add --transport http plinyville http://localhost:50592/mcp/all
all.tool_count: 15 corpus tools + one per repo (47 today)
all.what: one MCP server for the whole market: the pv_* corpus tools plus one tool per elder-plinius repo, named after it (pv_l1b3rt4s, pv_cl4r1t4s …). Each repo tool takes op=readme|tree|file|search|info|install|run|build and reads the archived copy when installed, live from GitHub otherwise; op=search archives the repo first if it has to.

mcp.per_mod: each installed mod also serves its own MCP server at POST /api/plinyville/m/<repo>/mcp (tools: <slug>_info, _readme, _tree, _file, _search, _install)
mcp.scope: PLINYVILLE_SCOPE=<repo,repo,…> starts a server that may only read those repos: every listing filters and every read refuses with "out of scope". That is how the chat fences a typed question — on the tool, not in the prompt.

name: pliny

does: re-pull the repo list from GitHub
refresh the plinyworld upstream snapshot (index.html + triggers.js + COMMIT)
restock installed market mods whose repo moved (cap 8/scan)
re-register the module and record the CID that comes back
scan.freshness: up to date for 36h after a good scan (24h interval + slack); then the pill says stale
scan.job: cron: 17 4 * * * — one scan a day (m pliny/cron [hour=] / m pliny/uncron)
scan.surfaces: GET /status · pv_status (MCP) · m pliny/scan_status · the header pill

run.note: a third of the corpus is a browser app, not prose. RUN serves those from their clone with Content-Security-Policy: sandbox and no allow-same-origin, so the page gets an opaque origin and cannot reach this host’s shared localStorage — on a direct link as well as inside the console’s iframe. Nothing executes on the server.

defanged.elder-plinius.github.io: the live clipboard-hijack PoC never runs from here; its RUN points at /plinyville the defanged exhibit

run.not_runnable: repos that cannot run say why: source that needs a build, a front end for a service that is not in the repo, a corpus of prompts
run.health: a page can serve 200 and still be dead, so the arcade says which: an unresolved merge conflict is repaired on the way out and announced in the file (stray half-markers too), a script that still will not compile is reported with `node --check`’s own SyntaxError, and a page whose back end is a service on localhost says which port it wants. A `const X` that shadows the enclosing function’s own parameter `X` is the other SyntaxError that kills a whole file (R00TS, dead since upstream wrote it): node names the line, the keyword is dropped so the line assigns instead of redeclares, node is asked again, and the repair is announced in the served bytes — R00TS now runs.
run.build: a few of these repos ARE apps but ship as source — the committed index.html is a Vite stub whose only script is /src/main.tsx, which a browser loads as a blank page. BUILD runs the repo’s own build inside its clone (npm install --ignore-scripts, then `vite build --base ./` or the declared build script) and the arcade then finds the built page and serves it from the same sandbox. GL4SS and P4RS3LT0NGV3 are playable this way; LEAKHUB is refused before it starts, because its bundle reads VITE_CONVEX_URL at boot and would build into a page that throws. Receipts in ~/.mod/pliny/builds.json carry the commit, the node and the log tail; a build whose clone has since moved is reported stale, not silently served.

types.what: forty-seven repos arrive as one wall of cartridges, and L1B3RT4S and AutoTemp are not the same kind of object. Every repo carries one or more types, and every listing takes ?type= (comma-separated = AND: type=jailbreak,app is a jailbreak you can also press RUN on).
types.how: a heuristic over the name, description, topics, README and filenames, PLUS what run.py measured (a page we watched load is an app, whatever its README says) and eight hand-pinned repos whose prose does not describe them. Every type carries its evidence — the word and the field it was found in — at GET /types?repo=<name>.
types.cache: ~/.mod/pliny/kinds.json (rebuilt per repo when its archive or clone moves)
types.surfaces: GET /types · ?type= on /repos, /market, /run · pv_types + type= on pv_repos/pv_market/pv_run · m pliny/types · the console’s pill row

chat.what: ask the corpus a question and let the CLAUDE AGENT do the reading. The headless `claude` CLI runs against this module’s own MCP server and answers with the repo and path it read it in.
chat.sandbox: claude --print --restricted --tools "" --mcp-config <this module> --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools mcp__pliny__pv_* — no Bash, no file tools, no WebFetch, no other MCP server, and only the eleven read-only tools.
chat.scope: types=[…] sets PLINYVILLE_SCOPE on that MCP server, so a jailbreak-scoped question cannot open anything else: the tool refuses ("out of scope"), and a filtered listing says how many it hid so the agent never reports "not found".
chat.honesty: the answer carries every tool call it made; one that never opened a file comes back grounded:false and the console says so.
chat.session: each answer returns the claude session id; pass it back as `session` to continue
chat.limits: 12 questions an hour per address, 2 at a time, 300s each (PLINYVILLE_CHAT_RATE / _CONCURRENCY / _TIMEOUT); PLINYVILLE_CHAT_TOKEN as a Bearer lifts the hourly cap
chat.needs: the `claude` CLI on the host, logged in. GET /chat says so when it is missing.
chat.surfaces: POST /chat · POST /chat/stream (SSE) · GET /chat + /.well-known/agent.json · m pliny/chat "…" types=jailbreak · the console’s ASK panel
